title: The Channel Tunnel
visual_consistency: A continuous semi-realistic educational illustration style with a recurring sea-map and undersea tunnel motif across all four frames. Use cool sea blues, muted engineering greys, and warm human details. Early frames use nineteenth-century engineering paper and model-table atmosphere; the final frame introduces a clean modern undersea train tunnel. Aime Thome de Gamond appears as a nineteenth-century French engineer, middle-aged, neat moustache, dark formal coat, carrying rolled plans. William Low appears as a nineteenth-century English engineer, middle-aged, calm technical presence, formal suit. Images must contain no readable text, no labels, no captions, no signs, no plaques, no readable maps, no speech bubbles, and no fake writing.
